question: Is an independently known positive beginning-cut mass paired with the action charge, on the same preparation, with a vacuum zero?
vacua: Keep positive outer packets, empty the seven interior densities and inject zero flow.
For a separate dust-free control set all dust density weights to zero, retaining order and clocks.
conditional_standard: Inject a known positive conserved flow from collar 3 to 7 along a saturated chain 3→a→b→7. Retain types with a minimal and b maximal with exactly one inner predecessor a. Link the two interior integrated density weights to the same marked flow using midpoint residence time on [T3,T7]. Flux readout is the published cut mass; action readout is its independent symmetric source difference at frozen fields. This occupation rule is an extra candidate matching, not a consequence of the action.
placement: D=T7−T3. Place b at fraction k of D and a at fraction 1/2−k. Keep the two proper-time cells of widths D/4 and 3D/4, the flux, boundary data, scalar preparation and geometry the same.
readouts: Exact sign and vacuum comparisons at both outer clock-lobe centers.
Uniform diagonal auxiliary expectation with the whole published two-lobe clock packet and half-width 1/32; check common 2% gain intervals and held-out mass without retuning.

On the first eligible canonical type compute the coupled dust source phase response with both coherent outer lobes and both density windows. All other clocks are set independently of charge in a linear extension. Fixed-order scalar factor is independent of dust fields for the published minimal joint action.
scope: Check the actual upstream physical run/independent standards. A candidate tagged standard does not by itself calibrate the original CST physical mass. Report unsupported fields as null.
